facts.d: Legislative terms were extended from five to six years, and the Lok Sabha elected in 1971 got an extra year — deferring the 1976 general election entirely. The 44th Amendment reversed the term extension in 1978.

facts.t: Four subjects moved from the State List to the Concurrent List
facts.d: Education, forests, weights and measures, and the protection of wild animals and birds. All four remain concurrent today — one of the few structural changes from 1976 that was never undone.

facts.t: Fundamental Duties came from the Soviet Constitution
facts.d: Part IV-A was modelled on the USSR's constitutional treatment of citizen obligations. It survived the reversals of 1977 and 1978 intact, as did the tribunals provisions in Articles 323A and 323B.

bank.q: With reference to the 42nd Amendment, consider the following statements:
s: It inserted socialist, secular and integrity into the Preamble.
It added Part IV-A containing ten Fundamental Duties.
It extended legislative terms from five to six years.
bank.e: All three are correct. The term extension was reversed by the 44th Amendment; the other two survive.

bank.q: Which one of the following changes made by the 42nd Amendment survives today?
o: Article 368(5) removing all limits on constituent power
Article 257A permitting central forces without state consent
Article 226A barring High Courts from examining Central law
bank.e: The tribunals provisions survive and were operationalised by the 1985 Act. The other three were struck down or omitted.

bank.q: Match List I (provision inserted in 1976) with List II (how it was undone):
pairs: 4. Reverted to five years by the 44th Amendment
bank.e: Judicial reversal for Article 368(4), the 43rd Amendment for the jurisdiction bars, and the 44th for the term and for Article 257A.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about Article 31C after 1976:
s: The 42nd Amendment extended its protection to all Directive Principles.
Minerva Mills struck down that extension.
Only the pre-42nd position covering Articles 39(b) and (c) survives, and remains judicially reviewable.
bank.e: All three are correct — the sequence that defines the modern relationship between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles.

bank.as: The 42nd Amendment represents the high-water mark of parliamentary sovereignty in India.
bank.rs: Articles 368(4) and (5) sought to place all amendments beyond judicial review and to remove every limit on constituent power.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — a direct legislative attempt to nullify Kesavananda, which Minerva Mills defeated.

bank.q: Which amendment removed internal disturbance as a ground for National Emergency?
bank.e: The 44th Amendment, 1978, replacing it with the narrower and more objective ground of armed rebellion.

bank.q: All of the following restrictions on judicial review were introduced in 1976 EXCEPT:
o: Article 144A requiring a special majority to strike down a Central law
Article 131A giving the Supreme Court exclusive jurisdiction over Central law validity
Article 228A restricting High Courts on state laws
bank.e: Article 143 is original to the Constitution. The other three were 1976 insertions, all omitted by the 43rd Amendment.

bank.q: Consider the following provisions added by the 42nd Amendment that remain in force:
s: Article 39A on equal justice and free legal aid.
Article 43A on workers' participation in management.
Article 74(1) making the President explicitly bound by ministerial advice.
bank.e: All three survive. The 44th Amendment modified Article 74(1) only to permit one reconsideration.

bank.q: Which case cemented the Basic Structure doctrine in response to the 42nd Amendment?
bank.e: Minerva Mills (1980), striking down Articles 368(4) and (5) and holding that limited amending power is itself a basic feature.

bank.q: Arrange the following in correct chronological order:
bank.e: Kesavananda (1973) → the 42nd Amendment (1976) → the 44th Amendment (1978) → Minerva Mills (1980).

bank.as: The 42nd Amendment tilted Indian federalism towards the Centre.
bank.rs: It moved education, forests, weights and measures, and protection of wild animals and birds from the State List to the Concurrent List.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — and unlike most of the amendment, this change was never reversed.
